source.title: Systematic Review and Inventory of Theory of Mind Measures for Young Children
source.extraction_notes: Sub-abilities extracted from Table 2 (pages 8-9 of the PDF in this repo). Descriptions are lightly cleaned for readability.

sub_abilities.name: Typical emotional reactions
sub_abilities.description: Inferring a person's emotional reactions based on situations that typically elicit certain emotions, or inferring a preceding event based on a person's emotional reaction.

sub_abilities.name: Atypical emotional reactions
sub_abilities.description: Inferring or explaining a person's emotional reactions based on situations eliciting emotions that are atypical compared to what is usually expected.

sub_abilities.name: Discrepant emotions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that people may have discrepant feelings about an event.

sub_abilities.name: Mixed emotions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that people may feel mixed emotions or different emotions successively.

sub_abilities.name: Hidden emotions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that other people may hide their emotions.

sub_abilities.name: Moral emotions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that negative feelings might arise following a reprehensible action.

sub_abilities.name: Emotion regulation
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that others might use strategies to regulate their emotions.

sub_abilities.name: Comprehensive emotion understanding
sub_abilities.description: Comprehensive measure involving emotion understanding based on different factors/ToM categories (e.g., desires, beliefs, hiding emotions).

sub_abilities.name: Discrepant desires
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that different people may have discrepant desires.

sub_abilities.name: Multiple desires
sub_abilities.description: Understanding the co-existence of multiple desires simultaneously or successively in one person.

sub_abilities.name: Desires influence emotions and actions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that people's emotions and actions are influenced by their desires/preferences.

sub_abilities.name: Desire-action contradiction
sub_abilities.description: Producing plausible explanations when actions contradict stated desires/preferences.

sub_abilities.name: Completion of failed actions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding another person's intent, as demonstrated by completing their failed action.

sub_abilities.name: Discrepant intentions
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that identical actions/results can be achieved with different intentions.

sub_abilities.name: Prediction of actions
sub_abilities.description: Predicting people's actions based on their intentions.

sub_abilities.name: Intention attribution to visual figures
sub_abilities.description: Tendency to attribute intentions to ambiguous visual figures.

sub_abilities.name: Intentions explanations
sub_abilities.description: Producing plausible intention explanations for different types of observed social events.

sub_abilities.name: Simple visual perspective taking
sub_abilities.description: Acknowledging that others have different visual percepts and adopting the visual perspective of another person.

sub_abilities.name: Complex visual perspective taking
sub_abilities.description: Adopting another person's visual perspective in tasks demanding complex mental rotation or visualization.

sub_abilities.name: Percept-action link
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that others' actions are linked to their visual percepts.

sub_abilities.name: Auditory perspective taking
sub_abilities.description: Considering the auditory percepts of another person.

sub_abilities.name: Knowledge-pretend play links
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone who does not know something exists cannot engage in pretend play that incorporates that knowledge.

sub_abilities.name: Percepts-knowledge links
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone who does not have access to perceptual information (by looking, hearing, etc.) may not have access to knowledge.

sub_abilities.name: Information-knowledge links
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone who was not informed or is not familiar with something may not know.

sub_abilities.name: Knowledge-attention links
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that something new is more interesting to someone than something already known.

sub_abilities.name: Content false beliefs
sub_abilities.description: Familiar container with an unexpected content: understanding the false belief held by someone who never opened the container.

sub_abilities.name: Location false beliefs
sub_abilities.description: Unseen change: understanding the false belief held by someone who did not witness or was not informed of a displacement or change of action.

sub_abilities.name: Identity false beliefs
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that when something looks/sounds/smells like something else, a person may hold a false belief about its identity.

sub_abilities.name: Second-order belief
sub_abilities.description: Understanding the second-order belief or false belief held by someone who does not know somebody else was informed (e.g., of a misleading identity or location).

sub_abilities.name: Beliefs based action/emotions
sub_abilities.description: Predicting another's emotions or actions based on their stated beliefs, or inferring another person's belief based on their stated action or emotion.

sub_abilities.name: Sequence false beliefs
sub_abilities.description: Understanding the false belief created when a predictable sequence of stimuli is broken with the intrusion of an unexpected stimulus.

sub_abilities.name: Comprehensive understanding of beliefs
sub_abilities.description: Composite measures of understanding beliefs (e.g., batteries of ToM tasks).

sub_abilities.name: Irony/sarcasm
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that other people may lie in order to be ironic or sarcastic.

sub_abilities.name: Egocentric lies
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone may consciously lie in order to avoid a problem or to get their way.

sub_abilities.name: White lies
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone may lie in order to spare another's feelings.

sub_abilities.name: Involuntary lies
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone may tell a 'lie' without knowing.

sub_abilities.name: Humor
sub_abilities.description: Understanding that someone may tell a 'lie' in order to make a joke.

sub_abilities.name: Faux pas
sub_abilities.description: Ability to recognize faux-pas (social gaffe) situations.

sub_abilities.name: Composite non-literal communication
sub_abilities.description: Measures tapping multiple aspects of mentalistic understanding of non-literal communication (e.g., Strange Stories).
